english.heading: Plant Selection and Guilds
body: Choose plants that work together—and change the planting as it grows.

body.text: Hlawula swimila leswi tirhaka swin'we—kutani u cinca ku byala loko swi ya swi kula.
body.backTranslation: Choose plants that work together—and then change the planting as they keep growing.

english.heading: Plant Selection and Guilds
body: A fruit tree needs light, water, soil nutrients and room. Support plants can supply food, leafy mulch, flowers and living cover.  Give each plant a useful job. Keep observing whether it helps the tree and the household. Which jobs does your planting need?

body.text: Murhi wa mihandzu wu lava ku vonakala, mati, nutrients ta misava ni ndhawu. Support plants swi nga nyika swakudya, mulch wa matluka, swiluva ni xifunengeto xa swimila leswi hanyaka. Nyika ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana ntirho lowu pfunaka. Tshama u langutisisa leswaku xana xi pfuna murhi ni ndyangu. Hi tihi tintirho leti ku byala ka wena ku ti lavaka?
body.backTranslation: A fruit tree needs light/sunshine, water, nutrients of the soil and space. Support plants can give food, leaf mulch, flowers and a covering of living plants. Give each plant a helpful job. Always observe closely whether it helps the tree and the family [?: ndyangu = family/household]. Which jobs does your planting need?

english.heading: Start With the Site
body: Find out what is limiting growth before choosing a plant.

body.text: Kuma leswi hungutaka ku kula u nga si hlawula ximila.
body.backTranslation: Find what reduces growth before you choose a plant.

english.heading: Start With the Site
body: Check sunlight, drainage, soil condition and water availability. Nitrogen is only one possible limitation.  Compare the soil beneath mulch with exposed soil. Choose support plants that fit the actual conditions. What does this site need first?

body.text: Languta ku vonakala ka dyambu, ndlela leyi mati ma hundzaka ha yona ekhatsi ka misava, xiyimo xa misava ni leswaku mati ma kona. Nitrogen i xin'wana ntsena xa swilo leswi nga ha hungutaka ku kula. Fananisa misava leyi nga ehansi ka mulch ni misava leyi nga funeriwangiki. Hlawula support plants leswi fambisanaka ni swiyimo leswi nga kona hakunene. Xana ndhawu leyi yi sungula yi lava yini?
body.backTranslation: Look at how the sun shows/appears [?], the way water passes through inside the soil, the condition of the soil, and whether water is present. Nitrogen is only one of the things that can decrease growth [?: 'ku hungutaka ku kula' = decrease growing]. Compare the soil that is under mulch and soil that is not covered. Choose support plants that fit together with the conditions that are really there. What does this place begin by needing?

english.heading: Give Every Plant a Job
body: A useful guild produces benefits you can observe.

heading.text: Nyika Ximila Xin'wana Ni Xin'wana Ntirho

body.text: Guild leyi pfunaka yi humesa mimpfuno leyi u nga yi vonaka.
body.backTranslation: A guild that helps produces benefits that you can see.

english.heading: Give Every Plant a Job
body: Choose members for food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or ground cover. One plant may do several jobs.  By the end, plan a guild, explain how residues feed soil, and decide which support plants to keep, cut or remove. Which job is still missing?

heading.text: Nyika Ximila Xin'wana Ni Xin'wana Ntirho

body.text: Hlawula swirho swa guild ku va swakudya, nitrogen fixation, mulch, swiluva kumbe ku funengeta misava. Ximila xin'we xi nga endla mintirho yo tala. Eku heleni, hlela guild, hlamusela ndlela leyi swisaleli swi phamelaka misava swakudya ha yona, u tlhela u endla xiboho xa leswaku hi swihi support plants leswi u nga ta ku swi hlayisa, ku swi tsema kumbe ku swi susa. Hi wihi ntirho lowu ha pfumalaka?
body.backTranslation: Choose guild members to be food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or covering the soil. One plant can do many jobs. At the end, plan the guild, explain the way the plants feed the soil, and also make a decision about which support plants you will keep, prune or remove. Which job is still lacking?

english.heading: Look for Root Nodules
body: Legumes work with rhizobia in nodules on their roots.

heading.backTranslation: Look for Nodules on the Roots

body.text: Legumes swi tirha swin'we ni rhizobia eka nodules etimitsini ta swona.
body.backTranslation: Legumes work together with rhizobia at the nodules on their roots.

english.heading: Look for Root Nodules
body: These bacteria convert nitrogen from the air into forms the legume can use.  Find nodules on a spare legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria and growing conditions. Can you find the nodules?

heading.backTranslation: Look for Nodules on the Roots

body.text: Magermu (bacteria) lawa ya hundzula nitrogen leyi nga emoyeni yi va swivumbeko leswi legume yi nga swi tirhisaka. Kuma nodules eka ximila xa legume lexi engetelekeke. Nodulation ni ku kula swi titshege hi ximila, bacteria leti faneleke ni swiyimo swa ku kula. Xana u nga kuma nodules?
body.backTranslation: These germs turn nitrogen that is in the air into forms that a legume can use. Find nodules on an extra/additional [?] legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, the suitable bacteria and the growing conditions. Can you find nodules?

english.heading: Return Leaves to the Soil
body: Nitrogen in plant material becomes useful as that material breaks down.

body.text: Nitrogen leyi nga eka swilo swa swimila yi va ya nkoka loko swilo leswo swi bola.
body.backTranslation: Nitrogen that is in the things of plants becomes important when those things rot.

english.heading: Return Leaves to the Soil
body: Return suitable leafy prunings, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.  This takes time. A living legume is not an instant fertiliser pipe into the fruit tree. Which residues can you return?

body.text: Tlherisa matluka lama tsemiweke lama faneleke, matluka lama wiseke ni swisaleli swa swibyariwa tani hi mulch. Swivumbiwa leswi hanyaka emisaveni swi humesa nutrients hi nkarhi wa decomposition. Leswi swi teka nkarhi. Legume leyi hanyaka a hi payipi ya manyoro ya xihatla leyi yaka eka murhi wa mihandzu. Hi swihi swisaleli leswi u nga swi tlherisaka?
body.backTranslation: Return suitable cut leaves, fallen leaves and the plant residues of crops as mulch. The living things in the soil release nutrients during decomposition. This takes time. A living legume is not a quick fertiliser pipe going to the fruit tree. Which plant residues will you return?

english.heading: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
body: Sesbania sesban can supply fast growth and leafy mulch.

heading.text: Sesbania Yi Ni Ntirho Wa Nkoka

body.text: Sesbania sesban yi nga nyika ku kula hi xihatla ni mulch wa matluka.
body.backTranslation: Sesbania sesban can give quick growth and leaf mulch.

english.heading: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
body: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this short-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant.  Allow room for its growth. Prune for mulch and reassess it when shade or water competition increases. Where could you manage its growth?

heading.text: Sesbania Yi Ni Ntirho Wa Nkoka

body.text: Yi indigenous eka KwaZulu-Natal. Eka swiyimo leswi faneleke swa ku fudumala, lawula xihlahla lexi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma kumbe murhi lowutsongo tani hi support plant. Siya ndhawu yo kula ka yona. Tsema marhavi ya yona ku kuma mulch, u tlhela u yi languta nakambe loko ndzhuti kumbe ku lwela mati swi andza. Xana u nga lawula ku kula ka yona kwihi?
body.backTranslation: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage/control [?] a shrub that lives a short time or a small tree as a support plant. Leave its place of growing [?]. Cut its branches to get mulch, and look at it again when shade or competing for water increases. Where can you control its growth?

english.heading: Check the Full Plant Name
body: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different species.

heading.text: Kambela Vito Leri Heleleke Ra Ximila
heading.backTranslation: Check the Full Name of the Plant

body.text: Sesbania sesban na Sesbania punicea i mixaka leyi hambaneke ya swimila.
body.backTranslation: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different kinds of plants.

english.heading: Check the Full Plant Name
body: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its pods have four lengthwise wings. Confirm identity using reliable botanical guidance.  Check the full name before planting. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban. Can the supplier verify the species?

heading.text: Kambela Vito Leri Heleleke Ra Ximila
heading.backTranslation: Check the Full Name of the Plant

body.text: Sesbania punicea i red sesbania leyi nga invasive. Swikhumba swa yona swa mbewu (pods) swi ni timpapa ta mune leti leha hi ku leha ka swikhumba. Tiyisisa leswaku i xihi hi ku tirhisa botanical guidance leyi tshembekaka. Kambela vito leri heleleke u nga si byala. Xixima project species list leyi pfumeleriweke, ku katsa ku sivela ka xin'wana ni xin'wana eka Sesbania sesban. Xana muphakeri a nga tiyisisa leswaku i xihi ximila?
body.backTranslation: Sesbania punicea is a red sesbania that is invasive. Its seed pods have four wings that are long along the length of the pods. Make sure which it is by using botanical guidance that is trustworthy. Check the full name before you plant. Respect the project species list that has been agreed, including any prevention/restriction on Sesbania sesban. Can the supplier confirm which plant it is?

english.heading: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
body: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—can provide peas, leafy material and nitrogen fixation.

heading.text: Pigeon Pea Na Yona Yi Nyika Swakudya

body.text: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—yi nga nyika tinyawa, swilo swa matluka ni nitrogen fixation.
body.backTranslation: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—can give peas [?], leaf things and nitrogen fixation.

english.heading: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
body: Use a sunny, freely draining position. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and waterlogging can limit it.  Decide whether each plant mainly supplies peas or leafy material. Frequent severe cutting can damage it and reduce the food harvest. Are you growing this plant for peas or mulch?

heading.text: Pigeon Pea Na Yona Yi Nyika Swakudya

body.text: Tirhisa ndhawu leyi nga ni dyambu leyi mati ma hundzaka kahle eka yona. I support shrub leyi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma; frost ni ku tshama ka mati emisaveni swi nga yi hunguta ku kula. Endla xiboho xa leswaku ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana xi nyika ngopfu tinyawa kumbe swilo swa matluka. Ku yi tsema hi matimba minkarhi yo tala swi nga yi vavisa ni ku hunguta ntshovelo wa swakudya. Xana u byala ximila lexi hikwalaho ka tinyawa kumbe mulch?
body.backTranslation: Use a place that has sun and where water passes through well. It is a support shrub that lives for a short time [?]; frost and water standing in the soil can reduce its growth. Make a decision that each plant gives mostly nitrogen or things of leaves [?]. Cutting it hard many times can hurt it and reduce the harvest of food. Are you planting this plant because of nitrogen or mulch?

english.heading: Choose for Place and Size
body: A useful support tree in one place may be too large or unsuitable in another.

body.text: Support tree leyi pfunaka ndhawu yin'wana yi nga va yikulu ngopfu kumbe yi nga faneleki ndhawu yin'wana.
body.backTranslation: A support tree that helps one site can be too big or not suitable for another site.

english.heading: Choose for Place and Size
body: Compare mature crown, roots, shade, rainfall and temperature. Check locally appropriate species and planting rules.  Put large support trees where they have space. For a small young guild, a manageable shrub may be easier to maintain. How large will this plant become?

body.text: Fananisa crown leyi kuleke, timitsu, ndzhuti, mpfula ni ku hisa kumbe ku titimela. Kambela mixaka leyi faneleke ndhawu ya laha ni milawu ya ku byala. Veka support trees leti kulu laha ti nga ni ndhawu. Eka guild yitsongo leyi ntshwa, xihlahla lexi nga lawuleka xi nga olova ku xi hlayisa. Xana ximila lexi xi ta va xikulu ku fika kwihi?
body.backTranslation: Compare a grown crown, roots, shade, rain and heat or shelter [?]. Check the kinds that suit the site here and the rules of planting. Put big support trees where they have space. For a small new guild, a shrub that can be controlled may be easier to look after. How big will this plant become, up to where?

english.heading: Annual Cover Has a Place
body: Sunn hemp can cover a suitable warm-season gap before the next crop.

heading.text: Annual Cover Yi Ni Ndhawu Ya Yona

body.text: Sunn hemp yi nga funengeta ndhawu leyi nga riki na swilo hi nkarhi wa ku hisa lowu faneleke, ku nga si va xibyariwa lexi landzelaka.
body.backTranslation: Sunn hemp can cover ground that has no things on it during a suitable hot season, before the next crop comes.

english.heading: Annual Cover Has a Place
body: Grow it where its season and space fit the plan. Its contribution depends on growth, nodulation and the material returned.  After cutting, allow for decomposition. An annual cover crop plays a different role from a longer-lived support shrub. When will this space be needed again?

heading.text: Annual Cover Yi Ni Ndhawu Ya Yona

body.text: Yi byale laha nkarhi wa yona ni ndhawu swi fambisanaka ni ku hlela. Mpfuno wa yona wu titshege hi ku kula, nodulation ni swilo leswi tlheriseriweke. Endzhaku ka ku yi tsema, siyela nkarhi wa decomposition. Annual cover crop yi endla ntirho wo hambana ni support shrub leyi hanyaka nkarhi wo leha. Xana ndhawu leyi yi ta lavekela rini nakambe?
body.backTranslation: Plant it where its time and place fit with the planning. Its benefit depends on growth, nodulation and the things that are returned. After cutting it, leave time for decomposition. An annual cover crop does a different job from a support shrub that lives a long time. When will this place be needed again?

english.heading: Leave Room Around the Tree
body: Keep the young fruit tree in light and retain access for care.

body.text: Hlayisa murhi wa mihandzu lowuntshwa wu ri eka ku vonakala, u tlhela u siya ndlela yo fikelela yo wu hlayisa.
body.backTranslation: Keep the young fruit tree in the sun [visibility], and also leave a way of reaching it to look after it.

english.heading: Leave Room Around the Tree
body: Keep an open establishment basin and access to the fruit tree. Place temporary support plants where their size and water use can be managed.  Put leafy cuttings where mulch is needed. Neighbouring fruit trees can share support strips between them. Can you reach both plants as they grow?

body.text: Hlayisa establishment basin yi pfulekile ni ndlela yo fika eka murhi wa mihandzu. Veka support plants ta nkarhi wo koma laha vukulu ni ku tirhisa ka tona mati swi nga lawuriwaka. Veka matluka lama tsemiweke laha mulch yi lavekaka. Mirhi ya mihandzu leyi tshamaka ekusuhi yi nga avelana support strips leti nga exikarhi ka yona. Xana u nga fika eka swimila swimbirhi leswi loko swi ya swi kula?
body.backTranslation: Keep the establishment basin open, with a way to get to the fruit tree. Put short-lived support plants where their size and use of water can be controlled. Put cut leaves where mulch is needed. Fruit trees that stand close by can share support strips that are between them. Can you reach these two plants as they keep growing?

english.heading: Build a Layered Support Guild
body: Combine seasonal cover, support shrubs and temporary small trees.

heading.backTranslation: Build a Support Guild Of Layers (layers)

body.text: Hlanganisa xifunengeto xa nkarhi wun'wana wa lembe, support shrubs ni mirhi yitsongo ya nkarhi wo koma.
body.backTranslation: Combine a covering of one season of the year, support shrubs and small short-lived trees.

english.heading: Build a Layered Support Guild
body: Cowpea covers sunny gaps. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can supply taller temporary support.  Add suitable flowering and mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk clear and manage light, water and access. Which layers fit your site?

heading.backTranslation: Build a Support Guild of Parts

body.text: Cowpea yi funengeta tindhawu leti pfulekeke leti nga ni dyambu. Pigeon pea yi nyika swakudya ni swilo swa matluka. Sesbania sesban leyi lawuriweke yi nga nyika support plant leyi tlakukeke ku tlula swin'wana, ya nkarhi wo koma. Engetela swimila swa swiluva ni swa mulch leswi faneleke. Hlayisa xikhuni xa mango xi nga funengetiwi, u lawula ku vonakala, mati ni ndlela yo fikelela. Hi swihi swiyenge (layers) leswi fambisanaka ni ndhawu ya wena?
body.backTranslation: Cowpea covers open places that have sun. Pigeon pea gives food and leaf things [?: leaf material]. Sesbania sesban that is managed can give a support plant that is raised/taller above the others, of a short time. Add flower plants and suitable mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk not covered, and manage light, water and access (way to reach). Which layers fit together with your place?

english.heading: How Many Support Plants?
body: Plan abundant support where the site and your care can sustain it.

body.text: Hlela support plants yo tala laha ndhawu ni vuhlayisi bya wena swi nga swi kondletelaka.
body.backTranslation: Plan many support plants where your place and your care can provide for them.

english.heading: How Many Support Plants?
body: Count woody supports across the spaces between fruit trees. Sow suitable ground cover by area.  There is no universal number per fruit tree. Adjust density to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin. How much support can you maintain?

body.text: Hlaya support plants leti nga ni swikhuni eka tindhawu hinkwato leti nga exikarhi ka mirhi ya mihandzu. Byala swimila leswi hangalakaka ehenhla ka misava leswi faneleke hi ku landza vukulu bya ndhawu. A ku na nhlayo yin'we leyi tirhaka eka murhi wun'wana ni wun'wana wa mihandzu. Cincela nhlayo ya swona eka ndhawu yin'wana ni yin'wana hi ku landza mati, misava, vukulu bya ximila ni vuswikoti bya wena bya ku tsema ni thinning. Xana u nga hlayisa support plants tingani?
body.backTranslation: Count the support plants that have wood [?: woody] in all the places that are between the fruit trees. Plant plants that spread above the ground that are suitable according to the size of the place. There is no single number that works for every fruit tree. Change their number in each place according to water, soil, the size of the plant and your ability to cut (prune) and thinning. How many support plants can you keep?

english.heading: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
body: Watch the branch fall onto the cut leaves.

heading.text: Chop-and-Drop ya Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu na Mulch
heading.backTranslation: Chop-and-Drop of Sun Exposure [?] and Mulch

body.text: Languta rhavi ri wela ehenhla ka matluka lama tsemiweke.
body.backTranslation: Watch the branch falling above the leaves that were cut.

english.heading: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
body: Prune a support tree and return suitable leafy cuttings to the soil. The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.  Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas. Which plant needs a cut—and how much?

heading.text: Chop-and-Drop ya Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu na Mulch
heading.backTranslation: Chop-and-Drop of Sun Exposure [?] and Mulch

body.text: Tsema tirhavi ta support tree kutani u vuyisela misava matluka lama faneleke lama tsemiweke. Vhidiyo yi kombisa rhavi leri tsemiweke: support tree yi ha yimile. Siya matluka lama hanyaka lama ringaneke leswaku xibyariwa xi tlhela xi tiyisa. Tsema hi ku ya hi muxaka wa xibyariwa. Papalata ku tsema ngopfu ku phindha-phindha eka pigeon pea, ngopfu-ngopfu loko u yi byala leswaku u kuma mimbewu ya yona leyi dyiwaka (peas). I xibyariwa xihi lexi lavaka ku tsemiwa, naswona ku tsemiwa hi mpimo wihi?
body.backTranslation: Cut the branches of the support tree and return to the soil the suitable leaves that were cut. The video shows a cut branch: the support tree is still standing. Leave enough living leaves so that the crop strengthens again. Cut according to the type of crop. Avoid cutting too much repeatedly on pigeon pea, especially when you plant it to get its edible seeds (peas). Which crop needs cutting, and cutting to what measure?

english.heading: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
body: Spread suitable cut material over the soil, with the trunk and root collar clear.

heading.text: Hlayisa mulch yi nga khumbi nsinya
heading.backTranslation: Keep the mulch from touching the trunk

body.text: Hangalasa swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke ehenhla ka misava, nsinya na root collar swi nga ri na nchumu.
body.backTranslation: Spread the suitable cut things on top of the soil, with the trunk and root collar having nothing on them (left bare).

english.heading: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
body: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.  Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition. Is the root collar still clear?

heading.text: Hlayisa mulch yi nga khumbi nsinya
heading.backTranslation: Keep the mulch from touching the trunk

body.text: Mulch yi sirhelela ehenhla ka misava, yi pfuna ku hlayisa mati ni ku vuyisela swilo swa organic. Siya ndlela yo cheleta mati ni ku kambela. Tsema swilo leswi tsemiweke swi va swiphemu leswi u nga swi lawulaka, u tlhela u ya emahlweni u languta mati ya le misaveni ni decomposition. Xana root collar yi ha nga ri na nchumu?
body.backTranslation: Mulch protects the top of the soil, helps to keep water and to return organic things. Leave a way to pour water and to check. Cut the cut things into pieces that you can control/manage, and keep going forward looking at the water of the soil and decomposition. Is the root collar still with nothing on it (bare)?

english.heading: Choose the Right Comfrey
body: Bocking 14 comfrey can supply cut leaves for mulch.

body.text: Bocking 14 comfrey yi nga nyika matluka lama tsemiweke yo endla mulch.
body.backTranslation: Bocking 14 comfrey can give cut leaves for making mulch.

english.heading: Choose the Right Comfrey
body: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.  Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree. Is this a good permanent place for the clump?

body.text: Kuma cultivar leyi lulameke. Bocking 14 a yi hangalali hi viable seed, kambe swiphemu swa timitsu swi nga mila nakambe. Yi byale laha ku nga ni ndhawu ni mati lama ringaneke. Tsema matluka loko yi ri karhi yi tlhela yi tiyisa; u nga yi tshiki yi phikizana ni murhi lowuntsongo wa mihandzu. Xana lexi i ndhawu leyinene ya nkarhi hinkwawo ya ku tshama ya xihlopha lexi?
body.backTranslation: Find the right cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again. Plant it where there is space and enough water. Cut the leaves while it is growing and strengthening; do not leave it to compete with the small fruit tree. Is this a good place for the all-the-time sitting [?] (permanent location) of this group?

english.heading: Observe Helpful Insects
body: Flowers can provide resources for useful insects.

body.text: Swiluva swi nga nyika swihlovo eka swinyenyana (insects) leswi pfunaka.
body.backTranslation: Flowers can give sources (of food) to helpful insects.

english.heading: Observe Helpful Insects
body: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.  Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control. What is the insect actually doing?

body.text: Ladybirds yo tala yi dya aphids; parasitoid wasps yin'wana yi hlasela swinyenyana leswi onhaka swilimo (pests). Swirho leswi nga ni swiluva ku fana na African basil swi nga engetela swihlovo. Languta swinyenyana (insects) leswi endzelaka ni loko ku onhaka ku cinca. Xihlahla lexi nga ni swiluva a xi tiyisekisi ku lawula pests. Xana xinyenyana lexi xi endla yini hakunene?
body.backTranslation: Most ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack insects that spoil/damage crops. Parts/members that have flowers, like African basil, can add sources. Watch the insects that visit, and whether the damage changes. A plant with flowers does not guarantee control of pests. What does this insect really do?

english.heading: Give Flowers Their Space
body: Wild garlic can be a flowering member where the site suits it.

body.text: Wild garlic yi nga va xirho lexi nga ni swiluva laha ndhawu yi yi fanelaka kona.
body.backTranslation: Wild garlic can be a flowering part/member where the place suits it.

english.heading: Give Flowers Their Space
body: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.  Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak. Where can flowers grow without crowding?

body.text: Tulbaghia violacea yi ni matluka lama nga banzi ni swiluva leswi nga ni muhlovo wa lilac. Byala xihlopha laha ku nga ni ku vonakala ka dyambu ni ndhawu yo kula. Languta swinyenyana (insects) leswi endzelaka. U nga tshembisi leswaku xirhendzevutani xa wild garlic xi ta tlherisela endzhaku swinyenyana leswi onhaka swilimo (pests) kumbe ku herisa ku hangalala ka swona. Xana swiluva swi nga kula kwihi handle ka ku phikizana?
body.backTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has leaves that are not wide and flowers that have a lilac colour. Plant the group where there is sunlight and room to grow. Look at the small animals/insects that visit. Do not promise that the wild garlic border will drive back the small animals/insects that spoil crops, or stop their spreading. Where can the flowers grow without competing?

english.heading: Bring the Jobs Together
body: Choose useful partners while protecting the mango's growing space.

body.text: Hlawula vanghana lava pfunaka loko u sirhelela ndhawu yo kula ya mango.
body.backTranslation: Choose helper companions when you protect the growing area of the mango.

english.heading: Bring the Jobs Together
body: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.  Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow. Does each member have space and a job?

body.text: Hlanganisa support functions leswi ndhawu ya wena yi swi lavaka: nitrogen fixation, swakudya, mulch, swiluva ni swimila leswi funengetaka misava. Swihlahla swin'wana swi endla mintirho yo tala. Siya ndhawu ya nsinya ni ndlela swi pfulekile. Kambela nakambe xirho xin'wana ni xin'wana loko mango ni swihlahla leswi tshamaka ekusuhi na yona swi ri karhi swi kula. Xana xirho xin'wana ni xin'wana xi ni ndhawu ni ntirho?
body.backTranslation: Combine the support functions that your place needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and plants that cover the soil. Some plants do many functions. Leave space for the trunk and a way (path) open. Check again each part/member when the mango and the plants that stay near it are growing. Does each part/member have a place and a function?

english.heading: Food Cover Also Competes
body: Sweet potato can cover ground and provide food in a suitable sunny space.

heading.text: Xakudya Lexi Funengetaka Na Xona Xa Phikizana
heading.backTranslation: Food That Also Covers and Also Competes

body.text: Sweet potato yi nga funengeta misava yi tlhela yi nyika swakudya endhawini leyi faneleke leyi nga ni dyambu.
body.backTranslation: Sweet potato can cover the soil and give food in a suitable place that has sun.

english.heading: Food Cover Also Competes
body: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.  Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Is this cover helping the tree establish?

heading.text: Xakudya Lexi Funengetaka Na Xona Xa Phikizana
heading.backTranslation: Food That Also Covers and Also Competes

body.text: Hlayisa marhavi ya yona lama hangalakaka ekule na murhi lowuntsongo wa mihandzu, u tlhela u siya ndlela yo yi hlayisa. Timitsu ta yona na tona ti tirhisa mati ni nutrients. Laha swihlovo swi nga ringani, fananisa swimila leswi hanyaka leswi funengetaka ni mulch basin ya ntolovelo. Xana leswi swimila swi pfuna murhi ku tshama hi ku tiyisa timitsu?
body.backTranslation: Keep its spreading vines far from the small fruit tree, and leave a way to keep/tend it. Its roots also use water and nutrients. Where sources are not enough, compare living plants that cover (the soil) with a normal mulch basin. Do these plants help the tree to stay by making its roots strong?

english.heading: First, Establish the Guild
body: Start while the young fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.

body.text: Sungula loko murhi lowuntsongo wa mihandzu ni support plants ta wona swi ri ni ku vonakala ka dyambu loku ringaneke ni mati lama ringaneke.
body.backTranslation: Start when the small fruit tree and its support plants have enough sunlight and enough water.

english.heading: First, Establish the Guild
body: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.  Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more. Can you care for every plant through establishment?

body.text: Byala hi nkarhi lowu faneleke, endla mulch u tlhela u hlayisa mati ya nkarhi wa ku sungula ku tshama endzhaku ka ku byariwa. Siya ndlela yo nghena yi pfulekile. Sungula hi nhlayo ya support plants leyi u nga yi hlayisaka. Languta ku hanya ni ku kula u nga se engetela. Xana u nga hlayisa xihlahla xin'wana ni xin'wana hi nkarhi hinkwawo wa ku sungula ku tshama?
body.backTranslation: Plant at a suitable time, make mulch and keep the water of the time of starting to stay (establishment period) after planting. Leave the entry path open. Start with the number of support plants that you can look after. Watch survival and growth before adding. Can you look after each plant at all times of the establishment period?

english.heading: Thin as the Fruit Tree Grows
body: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce selected support plants. Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.  Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition. Which support plants should now give way?

heading.text: Thinning Loko Murhi Wa Mihandzu Wu Kula
heading.backTranslation: Thinning When the Fruit Tree Grows

body.text: Loko ku tsema tirhavi ku nga ha ringani, hunguta support plants leti hlawuriweke. Tsema ehansi support plants leti phikizanaka leti hlawuriweke leswaku ku pfuleka ndhawu. Swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke swi nga siyiwa swi ri mulch: leswi i thinning hi chop-and-drop. Lawula ku mila nakambe leswaku ndhawu leyi pfulekeke yi tshama yi ri yona. Kambela ku vonakala ka dyambu, mati ya misava ni ku kula; thinning a yi herisi ku phikizana ka timitsu hi ku hatlisa. I support plants tihi leti nga fanela ku tshika ndhawu sweswi?
body.backTranslation: When cutting of branches is no longer sufficient, reduce the selected support plants. Cut down the selected competing support plants so that space opens up. Cut things that are suitable may be left as mulch: this is thinning by chop-and-drop. Control regrowth so that the opened space stays as it is. Check sunlight, soil water and growth; thinning does not end root competition quickly. Which support plants should give up space now?

english.heading: Move Support Into the Light
body: As shade increases, renew sun-loving support plants in open edges and younger plantings.

heading.text: Fambisa Support Plants Eka Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu
heading.backTranslation: Move Support Plants To Sun Exposure [?]

body.text: Loko ndzhuti wu engeteleka, tlhela u byala support plants leti rhandzaka dyambu emakumu lama pfulekeke ni eka swibyariwa leswintshwa.
body.backTranslation: When shade increases, plant support plants that like the sun again at the open edges and in the new plantings.

english.heading: Move Support Into the Light
body: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.  Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next useful sunny space?

heading.text: Fambisa Support Plants Eka Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu
heading.backTranslation: Move Support Plants To Sun Exposure [?]

body.text: Rhwala leswi tsemiweke leswi pfunaka u swi tlherisela eka mirhi leyi simekeke. Hlayisa swihlahla leswi nga ekusuhi ntsena laha swi ha tirhaka kahle kona. Mirhi leyi kuleke ya mihandzu yi ha lava nutrients. Languta ku kula, ntshovelo ni xiyimo xa misava; support plants a swi susi xilaveko lexi. Xana i kwihi ndhawu leyi landzelaka leyi pfunaka leyi nga ni dyambu?
body.backTranslation: Carry the helpful cut things and return them to the established trees. Keep the plants that are near only where they still work well. Grown fruit trees still need nutrients. Watch growth, harvest and the condition of the soil; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next helpful place that has sun?

english.heading: Let Observation Decide
body: Keep a short record of how the guild performs.

heading.text: Leswi U Swi Vonaka Swi Endle Xiboho
heading.backTranslation: What You See Made the Decision

body.text: Tsala rhekhodo yo koma ya ndlela leyi guild yi tirhaka ha yona.
body.backTranslation: Write a short record of how the guild works.

english.heading: Let Observation Decide
body: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.  Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here. What evidence would make you change the guild?

heading.text: Leswi U Swi Vonaka Swi Endle Xiboho
heading.backTranslation: What You See Made the Decision

body.text: Kambela ku kula ka murhi wa mihandzu, ndzhuti, mati ya misava, ntshovelo lowu pfunaka ni ku onhaka hi swinyenyana leswi onhaka swilimo (pests). Tsala leswi tsemiweke, leswi vuyiseriweke kumbe leswi susiweke. Tirhisa leswi u swi vonaka leswaku u cinca ndlela yo veka ni vuhlayisi. Xihlahla xi kuma ndhawu ya xona hi leswi xi swi endlaka laha. I vumbhoni byihi lebyi nga ku endlaka u cinca guild?
body.backTranslation: Check the growth of the fruit tree, shade, soil water, helpful harvest and the spoiling/damage by insects that damage crops. Write what was cut, what was returned or what was removed. Use what you see to change the way of placing and care. A plant finds its place by what it does here. What evidence is what makes you change the guild?

english.heading: Plan One Real Guild
body: Choose one fruit tree and mark a layout you can manage.

body.text: Hlawula murhi wun'we wa mihandzu u tlhela u kombisa ndlela yo vekisa leyi u nga yi lawulaka.
body.backTranslation: Choose one fruit tree and show a way of placing that you can control.

english.heading: Plan One Real Guild
body: Record the tree, site conditions and missing jobs. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave access.  Write down what will trigger pruning or thinning. Agree the species list with the project team where required. Can someone else explain your plan back to you?

body.text: Tsala murhi, swiyimo swa ndhawu ni mintirho leyi pfumalaka. Thya mavito ya support species hi ku helela, kombisa nhlayo yo sungula u tlhela u siya ndlela yo nghena. Tsala leswi nga ta endla leswaku ku tsemiwa tirhavi kumbe thinning. Pfumelelana hi species list ni ntlawa wa phurojeke laha swi lavekaka kona. Xana munhu un'wana a nga ku hlamuselela nakambe pulani ya wena?
body.backTranslation: Write the tree, the season of the place and the missing tasks [?]. List the names of the support species completely, show the starting number and also leave a way in/entrance [?]. Write what will make pruning of branches or thinning happen. Agree on the species list with the project group where it is needed. Could someone explain your plan to you again?

english.heading: Plant, Observe, Adjust
body: Start one suitable guild and care for it through its first stage.

body.text: Sungula guild yin'we leyi faneleke, u yi hlayisa ku fika emakumu ka nkarhi wa yona wo sungula.
body.backTranslation: Start one suitable guild, and look after it until the end of its starting time.

english.heading: Plant, Observe, Adjust
body: Use the right species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return useful biomass and protect the fruit tree.  Review the planting as crowns expand. Keep, cut, replace or remove each support plant when its role changes. What will you do first—and when will you review it?

body.text: Tirhisa species leyi faneleke, nhlayo leyi nga lawuriwaka ya swimila ni ndhawu yo kula. Vuyisa biomass leyi pfunaka u tlhela u sirhelela murhi wa mihandzu. Kambela nakambe ku byala loko crowns ti ri karhi ti anama. Hlayisa, tsema, cinca hi yin'wana kumbe susa support plant yin'wana ni yin'wana loko ntirho wa yona wu cinca. I yini leswi u nga ta swi endla ku sungula, naswona u ta yi kambela nakambe rini?
body.backTranslation: Use suitable species, a controllable number of plants and space to grow. Return helpful biomass and also protect the fruit tree. Check planting again when crowns are spreading. Keep, cut, change to another or remove each support plant when its job changes. What will you do to start, and when will you check it again?
